title: The Story of Saint Charbel
summary: Our flagship saint in the new storybook art style: ten sourced pages from the mountains of Bekaa Kafra to the hermitage of Annaya, with gentle read-aloud narration and points of reflection.
coverAlt: Painterly illustration from the new Saint Charbel storybook: a young mother with her small son beside a cedar tree in a Lebanese mountain village above the clouds

pages.title: A Boy in the High Mountains
pages.body: In a small village called Bekaa Kafra, high in the mountains of Lebanon, a boy named Youssef Antoun Makhlouf was born on May 8, 1828. His home was a quiet place of snow, cedar trees, and little stone houses, where families prayed together morning and night. When Youssef was only three years old, his father died. His mother Brigitta raised him with deep faith, and monks in his own family showed him what a life given to God could look like. Even as a small boy, Youssef learned that God stays close in happy days and in sad ones.
pages.prayer: Dear God, help me to be still and to listen to You. Stay close to me, and teach me to love You in small things. Amen.

pages.title: The Shepherd Boy's Secret Place
pages.body: Like many boys in Bekaa Kafra, Youssef helped his family by watching their cow out in the fields. The people of his village still tell how he would slip away to a little grotto among the rocks, a quiet cave where he could be alone with God. There he knelt and prayed, far from noise and hurry. It is a story handed down with love by his own villagers, not a scene anyone wrote down at the time. But it shows what Youssef loved most. Even as a boy, he was learning to listen to God in silence.

pages.title: A Brave Yes
pages.body: When Youssef was twenty-three years old, he made a brave choice. In 1851 he said goodbye to his mother and his village, and he walked to the monastery of Our Lady of Mayfouk to become a monk. Before long he moved to the monastery of Saint Maron in Annaya, where he received a new name: Charbel. In 1853 he made his solemn vows, promising a life of prayer, poverty, and obedience.

pages.title: Learning with a Holy Teacher
pages.body: After his vows, Charbel was sent to study at the monastery of Saints Cyprian and Justina in Kfifan. His teacher there was a wise and humble monk named Nimatullah al-Hardini, who would one day become a saint himself. Charbel studied Scripture, the liturgy, and the teachings of the Church with a quiet and listening heart. He was known as a student who worked hard, obeyed cheerfully, and spoke little. A holy teacher was helping to shape a holy student.

pages.title: Father Charbel
pages.body: On July 23, 1859, Charbel was ordained a priest, and he returned to Annaya as Father Charbel. For sixteen years he shared the daily life of his brother monks: their work in the fields, their simple meals, and their long hours of prayer. He rose in the dark for the first prayers of the day, and he gave his whole heart to the holy Mass. His brothers saw a man who was always obedient, always gentle, and always close to God. The hidden years were making him ready.

pages.title: The Little Hermitage
pages.body: In February 1875, Father Charbel received permission for something he had desired for a long time. He moved up the mountain to a tiny hermitage named for Saints Peter and Paul, where a few hermits lived in silence and simplicity. There he prayed deep into the night, fasted, and worked with his hands in the fields. He owned almost nothing, and he asked for nothing. For twenty-three years, that little hermitage was his whole world, and God was his whole life.

pages.title: A Story They Tell: The Lamp
pages.body: The monks of Annaya lovingly tell a story from those quiet years. One night, they say, someone playfully filled Father Charbel's lamp with water instead of oil, and the lamp went on shining all the same. This is a tradition, a story handed down with love, not one of the miracles the Church examined when it made him a saint. Still, it tells us something true about how his brothers saw him. They believed God was near to this gentle man, and his light did not go out.

pages.title: His Last Mass
pages.body: On December 16, 1898, Father Charbel was celebrating the holy Mass when he was struck by a sudden illness. His brother monks carried him to his cell, and for eight days he lay quietly, still whispering the prayers he loved. On Christmas Eve, December 24, he gave his soul to God, on the very night the world waits for Jesus to be born. He was seventy years old, and he had spent his whole life getting ready for that holy night. The next day, in the deep snow of that Christmas, the monks carried him to his rest.

pages.title: A Light for the Whole World
pages.body: After his death, wonderful things began to be reported. People saw lights shining over his tomb at Annaya, and pilgrims came from near and far to pray. Many sick people said they were healed after asking Father Charbel to pray for them, and the Church studied these reports slowly and carefully. On December 5, 1965, Pope Paul VI declared him Blessed. On October 9, 1977, before great crowds in Rome, he was declared a saint. The boy from a mountain village had become a saint for the whole world.

pages.title: Points of reflection
pages.body:
First, Charbel listened. He made room for God in silence, and we can do the same with a few quiet minutes each day.

The Bible says: "Be still and know that I am God!" That is Psalm 46, verse 11 (NABRE).

When could you be still and listen this week?

This week, take five quiet minutes with no screens, and just be with God.
pages.prayer: Dear God, help me to be still and to listen to You. Stay close to me, and teach me to love You in small things. Amen.
